stories.title: Reliance posts a record Rs 29,550 crore quarterly profit
stories.summary: Reliance Industries posted a record quarterly profit of Rs 29,550 crore for July to September, up 33.8 per cent, as its oil to chemicals business rode a surge in global fuel margins. Telecom growth offset a relatively subdued retail performance. Consolidated revenue rose 27.8 per cent to Rs 362,268 crore.

stories.title: GAIL profit more than doubles, gas arm heads for an IPO
stories.summary: GAIL's consolidated net profit rose 138 per cent to Rs 4,724 crore in the September quarter, from Rs 1,989 crore a year earlier, on strong gas transmission and marketing volumes despite geopolitical headwinds. The board approved plans to list its subsidiary GAIL Gas through an IPO.

stories.title: Bank of Baroda profit jumps 36% on its NSE stake sale
stories.summary: Bank of Baroda's net profit rose to Rs 6,532 crore from Rs 4,809 crore as non-interest income almost doubled, helped by Rs 1,340 crore from selling part of its NSE stake. Net interest margin slipped to 2.74 per cent. Owning a slice of the exchange paid off.

stories.title: Sun Pharma profit falls 36% as litigation costs bite
stories.summary: Sun Pharma's consolidated revenue rose 11.8 per cent to Rs 16,100 crore in the second quarter on growth in India and emerging markets, but profit fell 36 per cent as litigation costs hit earnings. Adjusted net profit was Rs 3,162 crore and the operating margin narrowed to 29.3 per cent.

stories.title: JioStar profit falls 13% in a weak ad market
stories.summary: JioStar's revenue rose 10 per cent to Rs 6,806 crore in the September quarter, but profit after tax fell 13 per cent to Rs 1,147 crore and EBITDA fell nearly 14 per cent. The company blamed a "weak ad environment" and said linear TV ad revenue remains "under transition".

stories.title: Jio Platforms reports 13.7% profit growth days after listing
stories.summary: In its first results since its record listing earlier this week, Jio Platforms reported a net profit of Rs 8,389 crore for July to September, up 13.7 per cent. Revenue rose 11.4 per cent to Rs 40,475 crore. New shareholders received their first report card within days.

stories.title: Lodha Developers expects to beat its full-year guidance
stories.summary: Lodha Developers' September quarter net profit rose 28 per cent to Rs 1,013 crore and revenue grew 18 per cent to Rs 4,468 crore. Pre-sales of Rs 9,670 crore in the first half are 40 per cent of its Rs 24,000 crore full-year guidance, which it now expects to beat.

stories.title: Inflation squeezes United Spirits' mass-market liquor sales
stories.summary: United Spirits chief executive Praveen Someshwar said the bottom end consumer of its liquor portfolio "is showing signs of fatigue due to the impact of inflation on their wallets." Net sales in its popular segment fell 22.7 per cent to Rs 181 crore. Pricier segments, he said, are holding up.

stories.title: Syrma SGS posts its best quarter as revenue jumps 73%
stories.summary: Syrma SGS posted record quarterly revenue, up 73.2 per cent to Rs 1,999.5 crore, while EBITDA rose 63.9 per cent to Rs 203.1 crore. Operating margins moderated to 10.2 per cent from 10.7 per cent. Exports, 26 per cent of revenue, grew 91 per cent.

stories.title: Tata Sons puts Rs 1,100 crore into Tata Electronics
stories.summary: Tata Sons has infused Rs 1,100 crore into Tata Electronics through a rights issue, company filings show. The unit makes iPhones through two subsidiaries and is building semiconductor assembly, testing and foundry capabilities. It posted FY26 revenue of Rs 1.31 lakh crore and a net loss of Rs 1,611 crore.

stories.title: Suzlon cuts its operating margin guidance to 15%
stories.summary: Suzlon Energy cut its operating margin guidance to 15 per cent after reporting an EBITDA margin of 15.1 per cent in the first half of FY27. CEO Ajay Kapur said the order book remains a healthy 6 GW and India's wind market will grow from 8 GW to 13 GW.

stories.title: Smartphone and TV makers plan 20% production cuts
stories.summary: Smartphone and television makers plan to cut production by up to 20 per cent after festive sales volumes fell around 25 per cent year on year. Rising memory chip costs pushed smartphone prices up 35 to 40 per cent and TV prices 20 to 25 per cent.

stories.title: EKA Mobility plans Rs 1,000 crore capex to push into trucks
stories.summary: Backed by an 11,000 bus order book worth nearly $1 billion including servicing, EKA Mobility plans Rs 1,000 crore of capital expenditure over three years for electric buses, heavy trucks and six-seaters. Chairman Sudhir Mehta targets Rs 2,800 crore in combined FY27 revenue across EKA and Pinnacle Industries.

stories.title: Mondelez adds 130,000 Indian outlets despite cost pressure
stories.summary: Mondelez chief executive Dirk Van de Put said Middle East driven inflation is a concern for consumers in India, but the company feels good about emerging markets. The maker of Cadbury and Oreo added about 130,000 outlets in India in the September quarter and sees plenty of room for more.

stories.title: India's services trade surplus rises to $53.39 billion
stories.summary: India's services trade surplus rose to $53.39 billion in the September quarter, as receipts of $113.029 billion outpaced payments of $59.637 billion, data showed. September had the biggest monthly surplus at $19.208 billion, against $17.647 billion in July and $16.537 billion in August.

stories.title: Fiscal deficit reaches 42.1% of the full-year target by September
stories.summary: The Centre's fiscal deficit reached 42.1 per cent of the FY27 target in April to September as total spending rose 10.7 per cent, CGA data showed. Major subsidies rose to Rs 2.23 lakh crore, with food subsidy up 16 per cent and petroleum subsidy down almost 83 per cent.

stories.title: Nifty reclaims 23,000 on October's last trading day
stories.summary: The Nifty 50 rose 0.51 per cent to 23,053 on Friday, back above 23,000 for the first time in eight sessions, and the Sensex gained 0.42 per cent to 74,459.53. It was a third straight gain, despite crude at multi-month highs, a global tech selloff and weak market breadth.

stories.title: Markets end October at a six-month high on a narrow rally
stories.summary: The Nifty gained 1.9 per cent in October on strong IT results and the Jio Platforms listing, even as Brent rose to about $117 a barrel and the RBI raised rates for the first time since 2023. Losses in mid and small caps showed how narrow it was.

stories.title: Intel falls 30% and takes the chip sector with it
stories.summary: Intel shares fell 29.9 per cent to $64.54 on weak PC demand and AI costs. AMD, Arm, Qualcomm, Nvidia, Broadcom and Micron fell between 2 and 9 per cent in premarket trading, and companies supplying equipment to the chip industry were hit too. The AI trade has discovered the bill.

stories.title: Wall Street slides on AI cash burn worries
stories.summary: US stocks tumbled on Friday, with the Nasdaq down 3.37 per cent at a three month low by midafternoon, Reuters reported. Results from Intel and Amazon amplified fears over AI companies' massive spending and when or whether the cash burn will start to pay off.

stories.title: Nasdaq 100 enters its third correction of 2026
stories.summary: The Nasdaq 100 fell as much as 4.5 per cent on Friday, completing a drop of more than 10 per cent from its recent peak and its third technical correction of the year. The earlier two came with the Iran war and a summer chip selloff.

stories.title: Nifty Pharma index hits a record high
stories.summary: The Nifty Pharma index hit a record 27,263.95 on Friday, up over 2 per cent in intraday deals, on a strong rally in contract development and manufacturing stocks. Mankind Pharma, Ipca Laboratories, Torrent, Divi's Laboratories, Cipla and Aurobindo Pharma were up 2 per cent each.

stories.title: Mid and small caps slip as Suzlon and Swiggy fall up to 10%
stories.summary: Mid and small cap indices fell up to 2 per cent intraday on Friday as Suzlon Energy, Swiggy, Sterlite Technologies and HFCL dropped as much as 10 per cent. The Nifty Smallcap 100 had surged 6 per cent in the previous four sessions.

stories.title: SEBI eases KYC reviews for foreign portfolio investors
stories.summary: SEBI has extended KYC review intervals for certain foreign portfolio investors from one year to two or eight years and removed a separate disclosure requirement, effective 1 December. The regulator said the changes reduce repetitive compliance. Foreign investors have been selling anyway, so the paperwork is at least lighter.

stories.title: SEBI fines CDSL Rs 1 crore for compliance lapses
stories.summary: SEBI fined depository CDSL Rs 1 crore for lapses including failing to tell depository participants why pledge requests were rejected. The regulator also flagged shortcomings in cybersecurity controls, vulnerability patching and disaster recovery drills. CDSL has been directed to pay the penalty.

stories.title: M K Sons Fine Jewels IPO subscribed 5.09 times
stories.summary: The IPO of M K Sons Fine Jewels was subscribed 5.09 times on the final day of bidding, led by non-institutional investors at 14.12 times. Retail investors bid 3.08 times and qualified institutional buyers 1.84 times. The price band was Rs 153 to Rs 162 a share.

stories.title: Silver's October losses reach nearly Rs 45,000 a kg
stories.summary: Silver's December contract on MCX fell another Rs 10,577 per kg on Friday to a low of Rs 1,79,600, taking its October fall to nearly Rs 45,000 per kg. The metal has given up more than half its 2025 gains. Gold fell to a seven month low.

stories.title: Forex reserves fall for a seventh straight week
stories.summary: India's foreign exchange reserves fell $1.3 billion to $719.8 billion in the week to 23 October, the seventh straight weekly decline. Foreign currency assets rose $1.4 billion, but gold reserves fell $2.7 billion, mainly because of valuation losses as gold prices dropped.

stories.title: Varun Beverages falls 5% after a 13.5% profit rise
stories.summary: Varun Beverages, PepsiCo's largest franchise bottler, reported a 13.54 per cent rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 830.6 crore for the September quarter, on double digit volume growth in India and abroad. Its shares fell 5 per cent on Friday. The market wanted a bigger fizz.

stories.title: Reddit shares fall 29% on a Google traffic warning
stories.summary: Reddit shares fell 29 per cent to $91.30 on Friday after it warned that declining traffic from Google Search could weaken user growth in the fourth quarter. It forecast revenue of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below estimates. The front page of the internet relies on someone else's front page.

stories.title: Why foreign investors keep selling Indian stocks
stories.summary: Foreign portfolio investors have pulled an estimated $65 billion from Indian equities since the market peaked in 2024, taking foreign ownership to a 15 year low, even as the economy grows and earnings recover. High crude prices and AI's threat to Indian services are among the suspects.

stories.title: November and December are the Nifty's best months, data shows
stories.summary: An analysis of 25 years of data by SAMCO Securities found the Nifty gains 2.5 per cent on average in November and 2.6 per cent in December. The index has fallen over 15 per cent in 2026 so far. History has been asked to repeat itself.

stories.title: Tata Motors takes control of Iveco for Rs 36,387 crore
stories.summary: Tata Motors took control of Italian truck maker Iveco on Friday, buying an 89.42 per cent stake for about 3.43 billion euros after settling its cash tender offer. The European business has annual revenue of Rs 1.42 lakh crore. Attention now turns to integration and repaying the acquisition debt.

stories.title: DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart for about $17 billion
stories.summary: DoorDash said it would buy Instacart in a deal valued at about $17 billion, pushing deeper into US grocery delivery. It follows Uber's $15 billion deal for Delivery Hero this year and DoorDash's own purchase of Deliveroo in 2025. Delivery apps are now mostly delivering each other.

stories.title: PE and VC investment in India rises 46% to $17.1 billion
stories.summary: Private equity and venture capital investments in India rose 46 per cent to $17.1 billion across 348 deals in the third quarter, the EY-IVCA report showed, though deal count fell 9 per cent. Thirty-six large deals worth $13 billion made up 76 per cent of the value.

stories.title: GRT Jewellers completes its takeover of TBZ
stories.summary: GRT Jewellers has completed its purchase of 74.12 per cent of Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri from the Zaveri family, taking full control of the listed jeweller. The Zaveri sellers no longer hold any shares and have been declassified as promoters, and TBZ is now a GRT subsidiary.

stories.title: Virat Kohli's Agilitas stake rises to 6.4% after One8 merger
stories.summary: The NCLT has approved the merger of Virat Kohli's sportswear brand One8 into Agilitas Sports, lifting his stake in Agilitas to 6.4 per cent from 1.8 per cent. Kohli invested Rs 40 crore in Agilitas last year and will stay on as co-founder of One8.

stories.title: Himadri to invest Rs 600 crore in Birla Tyres ahead of merger
stories.summary: Himadri Speciality Chemical plans to invest about Rs 600 crore in Birla Tyres to modernise and automate its Odisha plant, and expects the tyre maker to break even this fiscal. Himadri has proposed merging Birla Tyres into itself and expects approvals within this financial year.

stories.title: Aeroflex Neu takes 51% of valve maker Stilonn
stories.summary: Aeroflex Neu has completed the acquisition of a 51.01 per cent stake in Stilonn Valves and Controls, which makes stainless steel valves and fittings for pharmaceutical, food, dairy and biotechnology plants. Stilonn also supplies valves for liquid cooling systems used in data centres. It is now a subsidiary.

stories.title: Skipper buys Sansha Fastener for about Rs 15.5 crore
stories.summary: Skipper's board has approved buying all of Tamil Nadu based Sansha Fastener for about Rs 15.50 crore to expand its fastener manufacturing capacity in South India. The acquisition is expected to be completed by 31 December 2026.

stories.title: Inkle buys Finally's bookkeeping business
stories.summary: San Francisco accounting firm Inkle, which runs its technology operations in Bengaluru, has bought the bookkeeping division of Finally in an all cash asset purchase. About 100 employees join, taking Inkle's workforce to around 160. Financial details were not disclosed. It is Inkle's first major acquisition.

stories.title: Nelnet acquires Indian school software firm Entab
stories.summary: Entab Infotech has been acquired by Nelnet Business Services, a division of US company Nelnet. Khaitan and Co advised Entab and its promoters on the deal, Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas acted as India legal adviser and Baker McKenzie also worked on the transaction, Bar and Bench reported.

stories.title: Pharma M&A slows to 11 deals in the September quarter
stories.summary: India's pharma sector did 11 deals in the September quarter against 17 in the previous one, Grant Thornton Bharat data showed. Average deal size fell to $13.5 million from around $42 million, excluding the Sun Pharma and Organon tie-up. Buyers targeted brands, intellectual property and manufacturing capabilities.

stories.title: Family-owned precision engineering firms turn to private equity
stories.summary: Family-owned precision engineering firms including Hical Technologies, CTC Group, Balaji Precision Components, Gemsons and Rabwin are seeking private equity or strategic partners. CTC Group has mandated Avendus to sell a minority stake and raise about $50 million, and Hical wants a similar amount, people familiar said.

stories.title: Private equity sees promise in India's AI companies
stories.summary: India has largely sat out the global AI investment boom, but private equity investors see an opportunity, though public investors have few sizeable listed AI companies to buy. Goldman Sachs estimates IPOs over two to five years could add $50 to $100 billion to India's listed AI market value.

stories.title: Most healthcare private equity went to the west and south
stories.summary: A Brown University and Johns Hopkins study of 70 private equity backed acquisitions in India's health sector between 2007 and May 2025 found money went overwhelmingly to multispecialty hospitals in southern and western states. Over 73 per cent went to 45 hospital groups, while rural regions drew little or none.

stories.title: Anup Engineering buys a 10% stake for Rs 10,000
stories.summary: The Anup Engineering has acquired 1,000 shares, a 10 per cent stake, in the newly incorporated Arvind Global Capability Center for a total consideration of Rs 10,000, at face value of Rs 10 each. The new company will provide shared business services to group entities. Deals of every size count.

stories.title: NCLT clears the way for votes on a Cyber Media merger
stories.summary: The Delhi bench of the NCLT has directed Cyber Media Research and Services and Cyber Media (India) to convene meetings of shareholders and unsecured creditors on a proposed merger, under which Cyber Media (India) would absorb the ad-tech and data analytics firm. Secured creditors' meetings were dispensed with.

stories.title: Why SEBI wants you in direct mutual fund plans
stories.summary: Direct and regular plans of a mutual fund hold the same portfolio and fund manager, but regular plans bought through brokers carry distribution costs and a higher expense ratio, which reduces returns over time. Over 63 per cent of retail mutual fund assets still sit in regular plans, Mint reports.

stories.title: Why the IDBI Bank sale matters beyond its price
stories.summary: Fairfax is buying 60.72 per cent of IDBI Bank for Rs 52,878 crore, the government's most consequential strategic disinvestment since Air India in 2022, Forbes India says. Fairfax plans to merge Digit and IIFL Capital with the bank. The sale took years of regulatory, operational and investor hurdles to complete.

stories.title: What the Rs 10,000 crore container scheme is for
stories.summary: The Cabinet approved a Rs 10,000 crore Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme to raise India's annual shipping container capacity nearly tenfold, from around 70,000 twenty-foot equivalent units to 750,000. The aim is to create jobs and reduce dependence on imports.

stories.title: What an India-Mexico trade deal would mean for exporters
stories.summary: India and Mexico launched negotiations for a preferential trade agreement after signing terms of reference on 28 October. A PTA offers lower tariffs on selected products from member countries, which matters because Mexico has raised import duties on goods from countries without such agreements, Mint explains.

stories.title: How EPFO pays a fixed rate on market-linked money
stories.summary: EPFO invests provident fund contributions across debt and equity, yet declares a fixed annual interest rate. "Once the money arrives, EPFO doesn't decide what to buy on its own. The government notifies an investment pattern, and EPFO works within it," Trackk chief executive Vedant Gupte told Mint.

stories.title: CBIC tells GST officers to stop arrests now
stories.summary: CBIC has told its CGST field formations to stop carrying out arrests immediately and to apply the GST Council's recommendations on e-way bill inspections and show cause notices. The instruction comes months before the legal amendments were due to take effect. The rules arrived ahead of the law.

stories.title: E-commerce delivery GST falls to 5% from 1 November
stories.summary: From 1 November, delivery services for goods sold through e-commerce operators attract 5 per cent GST without input tax credit, down from 18 per cent, under a notification issued on 27 October after the 57th GST Council meeting. Postal and courier services are excluded from the change.

stories.title: IBBI rewrites real estate insolvency rules around finished homes
stories.summary: IBBI has amended insolvency rules for real estate to prioritise delivering homes, following the Jayanti Prasad committee's April 2026 recommendations. Creditors with at least 66 per cent of votes can now recommend excluding a project, with recorded reasons, and the resolution professional must then apply to the adjudicating authority.

stories.title: Why Jio Platforms is not a Reliance Power repeat
stories.summary: Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213 crore IPO overtook Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,806 crore as the country's largest and listed at Rs 1,358, a 21.36 per cent premium to the issue price. The analysis compares it with the Reliance Power IPO from the same family, which met a different fate.

stories.title: Why the Surat Diamond Bourse is still largely empty
stories.summary: Three years after it opened, the Rs 3,200 crore Surat Diamond Bourse, a nine tower complex that overtook the Pentagon as the world's biggest office space in a single project, is a largely empty shell, The Indian Express reports. It has hosted just two major events.

stories.title: Can a regular car run on E100? No
stories.summary: India has opened the regulatory pathway for vehicles designed for higher ethanol blends, including E100. Ordinary petrol cars have specific fuel compatibility limits, and only flex-fuel vehicles are engineered for different petrol and ethanol mixtures, Business Today explains, along with the difference between E20, E85 and E100.

stories.title: How paying employees to quit can keep the committed ones
stories.summary: Microsoft and BMW have introduced voluntary exit programmes that pay eligible employees to leave. Research suggests such schemes help firms reshape their workforces while keeping staff who are more committed, since everyone who stays has turned down money to go. It is a loyalty test with a cheque attached.

stories.title: Why Karnataka raised Nandini milk prices by Rs 8 a litre
stories.summary: Karnataka raised the price of Nandini milk by Rs 8 a litre from 1 November after demands from dairy farmers and milk unions. Rs 7 of the increase goes to farmers and Rs 1 to milk unions. Nandini still stays cheaper than comparable milk in several states.

research.title: The missing price feedback: Why studies overstate local grid peaks from synchronized home batteries under real-time pricing
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing studies consistently find that home batteries optimized against real-time electricity prices create new load peaks in local distribution grids. This is because all assets respond to the same price signal in sync. However, most of. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Tracks to Modernity: Railroads, Growth, and Civic Institutions in Denmark
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: We examine how railroads shaped Denmark's nineteenth-century economic transformation and the diffusion of Grundtvigian institutions. Using a panel of 1589 parishes and a difference-in-differences design for staggered adoption, we find that railroad connection increased local population. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: When Does Storage Complement Solar? Investment and Cost Recovery under Advanced Net Metering
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the joint PV and storage operational and investment decisions of a prosumer under net energy metering (NEM) and peak/off-peak tariffs. Legacy NEM compensates net exports at the retail rate over a netting period, typically. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: When are complements and substitutes dual?
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: For binary-action games on bipartite networks, strategic complements and strategic substitutes are one and the same: each can be transformed into the other by relabelling the actions of every player on exactly one side. In this. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Whom Do AI Agents Serve? Role-Induced Sponsorship Bias in Decision Models and Generative LLMs
research.summary: Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consumers increasingly delegate product search to AI shopping agents powered either by generative large language models (LLMs) that deliberate in natural language or by non-generative decision models that output calibrated choice probabilities in a single forward. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
